content: {"slots":{"fuel_phase":{"value":"gas","quote":"The experiment is conducted with gas-fueled flames, both with and without a coflow of air."},"gravity":{"value":"microgravity","quote":"The E-FIELD flames experiment investigates how electric fields influence the behavior of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity."},"flow":{"value":"forced flow","quote":"Parameters such as fuel flow rate, coflow velocity, and field polarity are were varied to isolate specific effects on ion production, flame stability, and soot behavior."},"atmosphere":{"value":"air","quote":"the coflow burner surrounds the fuel jet with a weak synthetic air flow to enable flame stability and soot behavior analysis."}},"functions":[{"function":"soot and smoke","statement":"The investigation evaluates soot formation, soot distribution, and soot volume fraction in electric-field-affected laminar diffusion flames.","quote":"High-resolution cameras captured flame shape, luminosity, and soot distribution. Spectral imaging with filters measures chemiluminescent emissions and soot volume fraction."},{"function":"extinction","statement":"The investigation includes stabilized near-limit lifted flames and dilution conditions extending to near-extinction flames.","quote":"Dilution levels were varied to explore a range of combustion dynamics, from highly stable to near-extinction flames."},{"function":"combustion fundamentals","statement":"The investigation examines how electric-field voltage relates to chemi-ion current, ion-driven convection, and flame dynamic response.","quote":"The objective of this investigation is to better understand the relationship between electric field voltage and chemi-ion current, analyze the dynamic response of flames to electric field changes, evaluate soot formation, and characterize stabilized near-limit lifted flames."}],"statements":[{"statement":"The fuels are methane and ethylene, each diluted with nitrogen to change flame strength.","quote":"Methane and ethylene were used as fuels and diluted with nitrogen to control flame strength."},{"statement":"Tests use a gas-jet burner and a coflow burner, with the coflow burner the same as in the CLD Flame experiment.","quote":"In the former case, the tests are conducted using the same coflow burner used by the Coflow Laminar Diffusion (CLD) Flame experiment."},{"statement":"The electric field is produced by a voltage difference of up to 10 kV between the burner and a downstream flat circular mesh.","quote":"An electric field is generated by creating a high voltage (up to 10 kV) differential between the burner and a flat circular mesh suspended above (i.e., downstream of) the burner."},{"statement":"Reported measurements include ion current, response time to electric forcing, flame shape and luminosity, chemiluminescent emissions, soot volume fraction, and radiant emissions.","quote":"Measurements, as a function of the field strength and fuel, are taken of the ion current through the flame and the flame’s response time to electric forcing."},{"statement":"All tests were run in the Combustion Integrated Rack on the International Space Station, with fuel flow rate, coflow velocity, and field polarity varied.","quote":"All experiments were conducted in the combustion integrated rack (CIR)."}]}
